1306:| `--access-token-env <VAR>` | One of three | Read the access token from an environment variable |
1307:| `--access-token -` | One of three | Read the access token from stdin |
1308:| `--refresh-token-file <path>` | No | Read a refresh token from a file, or `-` for stdin. Leave it out when you upload a fre
sh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects refreshes: stored, it only adds a long-lived credential |
1374:Expose a local MCP server through an MCPJam relay tunnel and register it as a server in your hosted project, so evals and stu
dies can target it. Requires an `sk_` API key or a prior `mcpjam cloud login`. The tunnel stays up until Ctrl-C; the server record
outlives the session (calls fail fast at the edge until you re-run, which revives the same URL slug with a fresh secret).
1399:> and disconnects any previous tunnel session for the same server.
1405:Grade a server locally — from your machine, against the URL you supply. No account required. Results are printed to stdout an
d never uploaded.
1486:`readiness check claude`, `readiness check openai`, `readiness start claude`, and `readiness start openai` all take these fla
gs. They let a readiness run grade a server that allows anonymous calls and asks for sign-in only on protected tools. See [Mid-ses
sion sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md) for the two challenge shapes.
1491:| `--lazy-auth-probe` | Opt in to the lazy-authentication probe. The probe calls one public tool, then one protected tool, bo
th **without credentials**. It makes at most two calls and calls only tools annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. Without the two flags
below, it picks the tools from their `securitySchemes`. |
1566:### `cloud eval create`
1568:Create a runnable eval suite from authored test cases (does not run it).
1573:| `--file <path>` | No | Path to a **create-API JSON** body (or `-` for stdin). A versioned suite file (`schemaVersion: "1"`)
belongs on `eval run --file` |
1579:| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Clients to attach the suite to (overrides the file). Without one the suite lists no clien
t, and `eval run --client` has nothing to select |
